problem: Whether the variance V alone forces a lower bound of order 1/V on the normalized Turán deficit δ_k = 1 − f_{k−1}f_{k+1}/f_k² near the mode of every Poisson–binomial law, which the paper settles at the first-descent index D by proving V δ_D ≥ 1/4 for V ≥ 1.
debate: Quantitative (Turán-type) lower bounds on the log-concavity slack of Bernoulli-sum pmfs (Hillion–Johnson, Johnson, Dümbgen–Wellner, Pitman), together with mode-location and maximal-mass results (Darroch, Bobkov–Marsiglietti–Melbourne), though the opening names no actual dispute, only a list of citations.
gap: Every known lower bound on δ_k depends on n, on the success probabilities, or on k alone, and all degenerate near the mode when summands with p_i near 0 and near 1 accumulate at fixed variance, so none is scaled by the variance.
contribution: A proof that V δ_D ≥ 1/4 with a binomial family showing the best constant is at most 1/3, the consequence δ_k ≥ 1/(4V + |k − D|) for all k, two-sided bounds at the rightmost mode, and an application to Haar-unitary half-circle eigenvalue counts, proved by combining cubic inequalities and a maximal-mass bound with an exact-arithmetic computer-assisted Bernstein expansion.
note: The statement is clean and the gap is concrete, but you never say why anyone needs a variance-scaled bound on δ_D beyond a normal-curvature heuristic, so move the unitary-matrix payoff into the introduction's first paragraph and state what the open gap between 1/4 and 1/3 costs.
